title: The terrifying tales behind some of Hampshire's most 'haunted' roads
excerpt: Drivers are being warned of haunted roads with chilling backstories and eerie sightings near Winchester and Romsey.
content:
Drivers are being warned of haunted roads with chilling backstories and eerie sightings near Winchester and Romsey.

With Halloween fast approaching, motorists are being urged to stay alert for spooky encounters along roads in Hampshire, where ghostly sightings and unexplained phenomena have been reported.

Twyford Down, now part of the M3 near Winchester, is steeped in legend.

In 1992, construction workers allegedly disturbed the graves of 18 unusually tall men, prompting claims of a supernatural curse.

Legend says two workers later died of heart attacks and a night watchman died at his post, prompting motorway opponents to call it "the curse of the giants."

A road outside the Old Forge in Otterbourne is said to be haunted by a woman killed by a horse and coach.

She is said to have been seen running across the road, while cries and raised voices have been heard inside the building.

Dark Lane in Braishfield is said to be haunted by an Edwardian woman searching for treasure she hid while living nearby.

Legend says dogs are more likely than people to sense her and may howl for no apparent reason.

An undisclosed main road in Bishop's Waltham was also the scene of a strange encounter in 1991.

Drivers should watch out for spooky encounters around Hampshire this weekend. (Image: Jamie Fielding)

Two friends reported meeting a woman dressed in black beside what appeared to be a Victorian bicycle.

She asked for directions to Dean, repeatedly replied "yes" and vanished after climbing on to the bicycle.

A road over the former Kit Nox Hill in Botley is also said to be haunted, but the ghost’s identity is disputed.

Some believe the ghost is local witch Kate Hunt, while others say it is Kate Knox, who reportedly drowned in a nearby pond.

In 2017, a driver reported seeing a white horse cross an unnamed road from Wickham towards Droxford.

Her passenger saw nothing, and when the driver reached the spot, there was allegedly nowhere for the animal to have gone.

The South West had 218 haunted-road reports, more than any other English region.

The East of England followed with 187 reports, ahead of the South East with 183.

The East Midlands had 109 reports, the North West 88 and the North East just 18.

Wiltshire, Dorset and Somerset recorded 151 reports between them, putting three of the UK’s five most haunted areas in the South West.

Have you witnessed paranormal activity on any of these roads? Tell us in the comments.
